title: extend service knowledge capabilities for docs like the infra telemetry wiring. must be done correctly and made sure no staleness risk
release-flow: dev integrates, main = stable release line (clone-safe for non-technical users)
description:
## PROBLEM

Three active repos under `~/dev/` — `specialists`, `xtmux`, `core` — currently merge all sprint work directly to `main` under PR protection. Non-technical users who clone `main` mid-sprint receive a half-done product: the branch tip tracks every dev merge, so a clone during a 20-PR sprint lands on an incoherent, non-shippable state.

Root cause: `main` is both integration target AND release line. No branch stays frozen between releases.

## SCOPE (agreed model)

Applies to all three repos: `~/dev/specialists`, `~/dev/xtmux`, `~/dev/core` (shorthand: `~/dev/{specialists,xtmux,core}`).

- `dev` = integration branch. All sprint PRs land here. Allowed to be half-done mid-sprint. Contributors target `dev`.
- `main` = release line, stays default branch (bare `git clone` hits stable code). Advances ONLY at release boundaries, not per dev merge. A release = "sprint done, verified" → merge `dev -> main` → tag `vX.Y.Z`.
- Non-technical users clone `main` → always get a coherent, shippable product. Half-done state lives on `dev` and never reaches `main`.
- Key rule: `dev -> main` = release. `main` does not auto-track `dev`.

## HOTFIX POLICY (decided)

Mid-sprint `dev` is unstable, so `dev -> main` merge is not viable for shipping a fix.
- Hotfix = cherry-pick to `main` as patch release (`vX.Y.Z+1`), AND land the same fix on `dev` for next sprint release.
- Chosen over `hotfix/*` branch + back-merge (lazier, fewer branches).

## WORK ITEMS (rough — refine when promoted from draft)

- [ ] For each repo in `~/dev/{specialists,xtmux,core}`:
  - [ ] Branch protection on `dev`: PRs required, required CI status checks, linear history.
  - [ ] Tighten `main`: only `dev -> main` merge PRs accepted; keep default branch = main; required CI.
  - [ ] Add required status checks (CI: lint + test) on both branches if not present.
  - [ ] Write one-page CONTRIBUTING note: PRs target `dev`; releases cut from `dev -> main` merge + tag; hotfix = cherry-pick to `main` + land on `dev`.
- [ ] Define release cadence guardrail per repo: do not let `main` go stale (stale main = different complaint, same dissatisfaction).
- [ ] Decide per-repo CI workflow details (stacks may differ across the three repos).

## TBD

- Per-repo CI stack details (specialists / xtmux / core may differ).
- Whether all three adopt the model in the same pass or phased.
- Release cadence per repo (may differ).

## CONTEXT

Filed under specialists:xtmux territory. Work to be done at a later point. Created as draft contract (contract:draft label) until promoted to ready before dispatch.

title: Ack git-cliff rollout: tune scopes + reconcile CHANGELOG
description:
git-cliff was rolled out across all ~/dev and ~/projects repos in one batch (8fabb93). This bead is the ack + tuning gate for THIS repo.

## WHAT LANDED
- changelog/cliff.toml — GENERIC type-based parsers only (feat->Added, fix->Fixed,
  perf->Performance, docs|chore|build|ci|test|refactor|style->Project maintenance,
  everything else->Other changes). Version-bump commits are skipped.
- header = "" on purpose, so the CHANGELOG keeps its own title and --prepend never
  stacks a second header on top of it.
- Commit links point at this repo's own origin remote.
- CHANGELOG.md: generated fresh if absent; otherwise --prepend --unreleased only.
  Verified non-destructive — 0 existing lines lost in every repo that had one.

## WHY THIS BEAD IS P0
The config is deliberately generic and is NOT tuned to this repo. Until someone acks it:
- Real work may be landing under 'Other changes' instead of a meaningful section.
- Scope names used by this repo's commits have no parser entry.

## TO DO
1. Run: git-cliff --config changelog/cliff.toml --unreleased  (inspect, do not write)
2. Count entries falling into 'Other changes'. If more than a couple, add scope parsers
   ABOVE the generic ones, e.g. { message = "^feat\\(api\\)", group = "API" }.
3. Document the scope taxonomy in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md so the agents that write the
   commits actually follow it — the taxonomy is useless if only the parser knows it.
4. If this repo had a hand-written CHANGELOG, reconcile the generated format against
   the existing style (they will not match).
5. Regenerate with --prepend --unreleased. NEVER use -o / plain generate on a repo with
   a hand-written CHANGELOG — it rebuilds from the git log and drops every hand-written
   line (measured: 362 lines would be lost in specialists).

## DO NOT
- Do not run git-cliff without --prepend on a repo that already has a CHANGELOG.
- Nothing was pushed. Review the commit before pushing.
notes:
RESWEEPED — config now renders commit BODIES, not just subjects.

The first sweep only templated {{ commit.message }}, throwing away the rich bodies the
agents already write. cliff.toml now renders {% if commit.body %}, so a changelog entry
carries the full rationale, bead id, PR number, and file/env details straight from git.
Verified on market-data: generated entries now match the hand-written ones in substance.

All changelogs were restored to their exact pre-sweep state and re-prepended.
Measured: 0 pre-existing lines lost in every repo that already had a CHANGELOG.

## REMAINING TUNING (this bead)
1. SCOPES — parsers are still generic (type-based only). Run:
     git-cliff --config changelog/cliff.toml --unreleased
   Count entries under 'Other changes'. Add repo-specific scope parsers ABOVE the
   generic ones, e.g. { message = "^feat\\(api\\)", group = "API" }.
2. COMMIT BODIES ARE NOW THE CHANGELOG. Document that in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md: the
   body is what readers see, so agents should write it for a reader, not a reviewer.
   Squash-merge commits currently dump the raw PR bullet list verbatim — verbose.
3. FORMAT — repos with a hand-written CHANGELOG have two styles stacked. Reconcile.

## HARD RULE
NEVER run git-cliff without --prepend on a repo that has a hand-written CHANGELOG.
It rebuilds from the git log and drops every hand-written line (measured: 362 lines
would be lost in specialists). Always: --unreleased --prepend.

Nothing was pushed. Review before pushing.
close_reason: Added per-commit date-time (commit.author.timestamp) to cliff.toml body; bodies already rendered. No scope parsers added: large fallthrough is unconventional/auto-backup commits with no clean taxonomy. Removed stale dead-hash Unreleased dump, regenerated with date-time; hand-written header + curated Unreleased preserved.

title: fix(service-knowledge): skill_activator decide() hard-blocks when the index is merely unimportable
description:
retrieve_evidence()'s docstring (skill_activator.py:182-184) states: 'available=False means the packaged index is not importable in this process (hook running standalone without the pip package) - that must NEVER block, only degrade to advisory. available=True, ok=False means a real retrieval failure (broken index) - that may block.'

decide() line 318 contradicts this: 'elif not retrieval.ok and not exempt:' blocks on ok==False without ever reading retrieval.available. The Retrieval.available field is dead code - nothing consumes it.

Observed in mercury-market-data: the PreToolUse hook is wired to system python3, which cannot import service_knowledge (only the pipx venv can), so every Write/Edit touching a registered territory was hard-denied with 'Retrieval failed: service-knowledge index not importable' - including edits to .gitignore and .claude/settings.json, which are not in any territory. That deadlocks the operator: the hook blocks the very edit that would repair the hook.

Fix: gate the block on 'retrieval.available and not retrieval.ok'; when available is False, return an advisory allow.

Secondary: territory matching attributed .gitignore and .claude/settings.json to serving-mcp-tools, whose territory is 'api/mcp_server.py, api/docstrings/**/*, api/toon.py, api/filtering.py'. Neither path matches those globs - investigate the fallback that picks a service when no glob matches.

title: fix(service-knowledge): make drift detection ref-based so isolated worktrees work
description:
drift_detector.py:250 selects drift with 'fp.stat().st_mtime > last_sync'. A fresh git worktree checkout restamps every file's mtime, so any isolated run reports the entire registered territory as drifted. Measured in mercury-market-data at one commit with identical content: 64 items in the live repo vs 166 in a worktree of the same HEAD.

Effect: xtrm-service-knowledge-reconcile.yaml had to be switched to worktree.enabled=false (it previously ran isolated and, combined with the tree being gitignored, silently reported ALIGNED against 64 real drift items).

Fix: select drift by comparing last_sync_ref..HEAD (git diff --name-only) instead of mtime, falling back to mtime only when last_sync_ref is empty/unresolvable. The service registry already stores last_sync_ref and service_knowledge_diff_scan.py already does ref-based diffing, so the machinery exists.

Acceptance: scan_drift() returns identical results in a repo and in a fresh worktree of the same HEAD; then re-enable worktree.enabled=true in the reconcile workflow.

- Scope reviewed: `origin/main...HEAD`, `packages/service-knowledge`, PR3 MCP/index/secret/hook paths.
- Overall risk: **high**.
- Modes: static secure-code review, MCP/config scan, dependency audit triage.
- Verdict: **fail**. Fix high path read before merge.

## Status
Findings: 2. No files changed.

## Findings
### SK-001 — High — Path traversal / arbitrary file read (CWE-22, CWE-200)
- Evidence:
  - `packages/service-knowledge/src/service_knowledge/mcp/knowledge_get.py:28-37` accepts caller `skill_path`.
  - `packages/service-knowledge/src/service_knowledge/index/query.py:369-381` builds `Path(consumer_root) / skill_rel_path`, checks existence, then returns raw `read_text()` content.
  - No repo-containment check. No `SKILL.md` allowlist.
- Reachability/exploitability: Any MCP caller able to invoke `knowledge_get` can submit traversal or absolute path. `consumer_root` also caller-controlled through `mcp/_root.py:14-16`.
- Impact: Read MCP process-readable files, including secret/config files. Fallback bypasses indexed-document secret scrubbing.
- Recommended fix: Resolve candidate path; require `candidate.is_relative_to(root.resolve())`; require expected registered skill path or strict `.../SKILL.md` allowlist. Remove raw filesystem fallback; return only scrubbed indexed document.
- Verification after fix: Tests reject traversal, absolute paths, non-SKILL files, alternate `consumer_root`; confirm no raw secret reaches MCP response.

### SK-002 — Medium — Secret scrubber misses Discord webhook assignments (CWE-200)
- Evidence:
  - `packages/service-knowledge/src/service_knowledge/index/secrets.py:29-43` covers Slack webhook only, credential URLs, JWTs, tokens, generic assignment names.
  - Generic assignment matcher excludes webhook URL variable names.
  - `builder.py:131-169` stores scrubber output in SQLite/FTS; `query.py:340-349` returns stored text through MCP.
  - Existing test `index/tests/test_secrets.py:22-26` checks Discord-named variable paired with Slack URL, so Slack-specific rule masks missing Discord format coverage.
- Reachability/exploitability: Secret accidentally committed in indexed SKILL content, then queried through MCP/index.
- Impact: Bearer webhook credential persists in SQLite, FTS, evidence bundles, backups.
- Recommended fix: Add Discord webhook pattern and generic `*_WEBHOOK_URL` assignment coverage. Add regression test using Discord-shaped synthetic URL; assert absence from every searchable layer and MCP response.
- Verification after fix: Rebuild test index; scan `documents`, FTS, `sk_items`, MCP bundle for synthetic value.

## Dependency Advisory Triage
- Package: `jsonschema`, `markdown-it-py`, `vaultctl`
- Installed version: unknown. No lockfile tracked.
- Advisory/source: none established.
- Reachability: direct.
- Recommendation: Generate/commit resolver lock or CI SBOM. Run `pip-audit` or `osv-scanner` against resolved environment. Local audit tools unavailable; `python3` import also failed because `vaultctl` absent.

## Non-findings / Dropped Noise
- SQL injection: no finding. User query reaches FTS `MATCH ?` parameter binding; dynamic SQL only creates placeholder count from internal mapping.
- Unsafe deserialization: no finding. Claim JSON uses `json.loads`; markdown frontmatter uses `yaml.safe_load`.
- Hook command injection: no finding. Hook passes list-form subprocess arguments. Auto-reconcile remains explicit opt-in, though it enables write-capable local scripts.
- MCP malformed JSON/object can terminate stdio process before handler catch (`mcp/server.py:18-20`, `34-45`). Dropped: local stdio availability-only impact, no remote route shown.

## Verification
- GitNexus flow/context: MCP `serve_stdio` → `handle`; `knowledge_get` → index retrieval; builder/query/schema/secret paths.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD -- packages/service-knowledge`
- Inspected PR commits through `3b36d59`, including `cf04056`.
- GitNexus change detection: no local working-tree changes.
- Read-only audit. No edits, installs, exploits, or dependency changes.

## Risks
- SK-001 exposes process-readable files now.
- Index retention stores missed secret formats until cache removal/rebuild.
- Auto-reconcile hook runs write-capable specialist when operators enable opt-in.

- Writer: fix SK-001, add containment and raw-fallback tests.
- Writer: fix SK-002, add Discord webhook scrub coverage and rebuild-persistence test.
- Executor: resolve dependencies in isolated environment; run vulnerability audit.

title: Epic: service-skills reframe — deterministic verifier + evidence-first retrieval
description:
## PROBLEM

Two failure modes prove the current service-skills machinery ships operational-knowledge risk unchecked:

1. **Blast radius on rewrite**: reconcile.py + service-skills-sync specialist generate rewritten SKILL.md and write immediately — no fact-check, no citation extraction, no completeness verification. A single specialist run recently shipped a SKILL section with invented redaction-key set, wrong redaction literal, mis-labeled metric-label set. Wrong SKILL becomes ground truth for every future session.

2. **Consumption gap**: SKILLs are barely used. skill_activator.py fires a 'please read this' reminder AFTER the tool call the agent already committed to. Nothing in bead contracts, specialist prompts, or issue dispatch demands service context.

Research (~/dev/xtrm/docs/research/kb-knowledge-base-svc.md, 975 lines, cited SOTA + shipping systems) recommends two derived layers on top of existing SKILL.md/registry/machinery:
- **Claim verifier**: deterministic Python between LLM output and any write/commit/PR; explicit gate lattice (INVALID / CONFLICT / EVIDENCE_RACE / INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_HIGH_RISK / PASS_WITH_ADVISORIES / PASS); PASS != auto-merge on day one.
- **Evidence-first retrieval**: per-repo SQLite FTS5 index + narrow read-only MCP tools; no answer() endpoint.

Given the scale + coherence of the reframe, machinery elevates to a first-class xtrm package: **service-knowledge**, home ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/. **Independent lifecycle**: its own CLI (`service-knowledge install|update|status|migrate|remove`) — NOT routed through `xt update --apply`. Rename from 'service-skills' → 'service-knowledge' reflects the reframe target.

## SUCCESS

At epic close:
- Auto-reconcile + specialist runs cannot ship SKILL with invented literals, wrong metric-label sets, invented env vars, or falsely-complete lists — verifier blocks BEFORE atomic_write.
- Every bead touching a registered territory receives an evidence bundle at dispatch; Write/Edit in registered territory blocks when bundle can't be built.
- SKILL.md remains authoring surface; registry stays source of truth.
- Machinery ships as first-class xtrm package (service-knowledge v0.6.0) with own CLI, own release cadence, own CHANGELOG.
- **vaultctl is a package dependency** (~/dev/vaultctl provides SQLite/FTS5/BM25 substrate — 897 LOC of proven store layer we don't rewrite). service-knowledge adds only the domain-specific extensions (items with kind=service|section|claim|probe|conflict, citations, retrieval_events, index_state).
- **mercury-infra is the PoC consumer** (17 services, richest fixture set). 6 other service-hosting mercury repos adopt when operator triggers each — no forced-wave.
- **~/dev/core and ~/dev/specialists are NOT consumers**. They are xtrm tooling repos, not service hosts. Nothing to index there.
- Federated cross-repo query via ~/.xtrm/stack-registry.json enables devops-agent-dispatched-from-infra to touch sibling stacks without centralized DB.
- 80-150-case labeled eval corpus + telemetry proves retrieval precision/recall, stale-claim escape rate, verifier FP/FN rates.

## SCOPE

**Package home**: ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/ — independent, own CLI, own versioning

**Package CLI** (new):
- `service-knowledge install` — first-time install in a consumer repo
- `service-knowledge update` — pull latest package version into consumer
- `service-knowledge status` — report installed version + index health + drift
- `service-knowledge migrate` — rename/schema migration (used in PR0 for the service-skills → service-knowledge flip)
- `service-knowledge remove` — uninstall (for consumer repos that deprecate)

**Consumer path** (in each of 7 service-hosting mercury repos): .xtrm/skills/default/service-knowledge/ (renamed from service-skills/)

**Per-repo derived index**: .xtrm/cache/service-knowledge.sqlite (NOT .beads/)

**Cross-repo federation surface**: ~/.xtrm/stack-registry.json (user-scoped)

**Consumer repos (7 service-hosting mercury only)**:
- mercury-infra (PoC #1)
- mercury-market-data
- mercury-darth-feedor  
- mercury-treasury-cb
- mercury-quant
- mercury-sierra-vps
- mercury-website

**NOT consumers**: ~/dev/core, ~/dev/specialists, ~/dev/xtrm, ~/dev/xtmux, ~/dev/vaultctl — xtrm tooling repos, no services to index.

**Dependencies**:
- vaultctl (as a Python package dep) — provides SQLite/FTS5/BM25/indexer/search/graph substrate

**Docs home**: ~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/service-knowledge.md

## NON_GOALS

- Not routed through `xt update --apply` — service-knowledge has its OWN CLI (`service-knowledge update`). Independent lifecycle.
- ~/dev/core and ~/dev/specialists are NOT installed — they host xtrm tooling, not services
- No new database service (Postgres, vector DB, external store)
- No LLM in retrieval hot path or as gate arbiter; no LLM-panel majority vote
- No auto-merge on PASS in initial rollout (canary decision in PR5b)
- No single centralized ~/.xtrm/knowledge.sqlite union DB — federated over per-repo indexes
- No embeddings (deferred until BM25 recall failure measured)
- No replacement of registry, SKILL.md, or Dolt-backed bd memory
- No general-purpose organizational KB, Slack connector, or auto-remediation
- No simultaneous rewrite of all 17 shipped SKILLs — semantic-markers migration is progressive
- No docs/ inside package on day one — add when first substantive doc lands
- No forced-wave migration of 6 other mercury repos in PR0 — operator triggers each when ready
- **Don't reimplement what vaultctl already ships**: schema.sql, indexer, search, BM25 tokenization, link resolution, in-degree graph, CLI-JSON scaffolding

## CONSTRAINTS

- Machinery lives in ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/; never migrate back to core.
- Package has independent CLI, independent versioning, independent release. NOT bundled with any other xtrm package's update cadence.
- Consumer set is ONLY service-hosting mercury repos. If a new mercury service-host repo lands, add to consumer list; core/specialists/tooling repos NEVER become consumers.
- vaultctl is a hard dep; service-knowledge does not reimplement its store layer. Domain schema extensions attach on top.
- Registry stays source of truth for service ↔ territory; index at .xtrm/cache/service-knowledge.sqlite is rebuildable projection.
- Deterministic before LLM at every gate; LLM steps produce advisory output only.
- Provenance model NOT ADD-only: active/superseded/invalidated + append-only history.
- Semantic markers hard-protected everywhere.
- Blocking hooks scoped tightly: Write/Edit registered territory + high-risk mutating Bash. Read/Glob/Grep never block.
- Package versioning: v0.1.0 baseline after PR0; +minor per merged PR (PR1→v0.2.0, PR2→v0.3.0, PR3→v0.4.0, PR4→v0.5.0, PR5a→v0.6.0, PR5b→v0.7.0). Reserve v1.0.0 for canary auto-merge activation.
- Logging/telemetry: every retrieval + verifier decision emits structured event to .xtrm/state/service-knowledge/events.jsonl. No secrets. No raw payloads.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Package released at v0.6.0 (or v0.7.0 with PR5b)
- [ ] `service-knowledge --help` works standalone; NOT routed through `xt update`
- [ ] vaultctl imported as dep; service-knowledge stores 5-table extension (items/citations/conflicts/retrieval_events/index_state) as an attached DB or migration
- [ ] All 7 mercury service-host repos CAN install (`service-knowledge install`); mercury-infra IS installed as wave-1
- [ ] core + specialists + xtrm + xtmux + vaultctl are NOT installed (validation: `ls ~/dev/core/.xtrm/skills/default/service-knowledge/` returns 'not found')
- [ ] Deterministic verifier catches all 3 failure classes from observed api-gateway/runners regression — golden fixture per class
- [ ] reconcile.py refuses atomic_write on CONFLICT/INVALID; draft-only PR on INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_HIGH_RISK
- [ ] Every bead touching a registered territory attaches evidence_bundle_id + evidence_hash
- [ ] Write/Edit in registered territory blocks when retrieval fails (with clear override path)
- [ ] Federated query via ~/.xtrm/stack-registry.json returns ranked results across ≥2 stacks with per-repo provenance
- [ ] Labeled eval corpus (≥80 cases): routing precision ≥ 0.8, retrieval precision@5 ≥ 0.6, stale-claim escape rate ≤ 0.05
- [ ] Verifier FP ≤ 0.05, FN ≤ 0.10
- [ ] Semantic-block protection: 100% preserved across every regeneration path
- [ ] Post-merge reindex ≤ 60s on all 7 consumers
- [ ] ~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/service-knowledge.md links resolve

## OUTPUT

At epic close, orchestrator publishes:
- Per-PR summary (merged SHA, key changes, coverage delta, package version)
- service-knowledge v0.6+ CHANGELOG
- Verifier golden-fixture report + regression classes
- Eval corpus stats
- Retrieval telemetry snapshot (7d after PR4)
- Federated-query smoke transcript (≥2 stacks)
- Wave-1 install evidence (mercury-infra); wave-2..7 tracking issue for on-operator-trigger installs
- Residual risks + follow-up beads (residual LLM critic if verifier FN > 0.10; session cache if activator latency > 200ms; centralized DB triggers; per-role ACL; remaining 8 claim types)
- ~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/service-knowledge.md updated with the shipped user manual

## REFERENCES

- ~/dev/xtrm/docs/research/kb-knowledge-base-svc.md — the 975-line deep research doc (§1-§7)
- ~/dev/vaultctl/ — SQLite/FTS5/BM25 substrate package (dep)
- ~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/ — home for operator-facing service-knowledge docs
- /tmp/deep-research-prompt-svc-skills.md — prompt that produced the research
- ~/dev/core/docs/design/memory-system-r6g.md — adjacent design (shared plumbing: FTS5, provenance)
- ~/dev/core/docs/service-skills-auto-reconcile.md — current Phase A + B runbook (migrates under the package)
- Sibling bead xtrm-y0tdg (Repo skills layout v2) — layout concern, keep separate
- Sibling bead infra-wtd1 (orphan-scan) — orphan-detection lane; ships in parallel; its service_skill_orphan_scan.py also moves into the package via PR0

## EXECUTION MODEL

All 6 (or 7 with PR5b split) PRs dispatch via specialists per /multiplexing + /using-specialists:
`sp run <specialist> --bead xtrm-56flm.N --worktree` on each. Parallelization:
- Wave 1: PR0 (blocks all) — solo
- Wave 2: PR1 || PR3 (both blocked-by PR0 only)
- Wave 3: PR2 (blocked-by PR1) || PR4 (blocked-by PR3)
- Wave 4: PR5a (blocked-by all impl) || PR5b (blocked-by PR5a for measurement inputs, else standalone)

Coordinator dispatches, monitors panes per /multiplexing message-send + safe-send-pointer, applies gate5 (reviewer PASS + merge) per /using-specialists rule #9. Target: ship in ~3-4 days with 2-3 waves running concurrent workers.

title: bootstrap.get_registry_path: probe <pack>/service-skills/service-registry.json (drift detector L0)
description:
## Problem

`bootstrap.get_registry_path()` at `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/bootstrap.py:118-155`
resolves the registry via 5 probes (env var → root symlink → pack root → legacy → create-at). The
pack-root probe (line 144) checks `<pack>/service-registry.json` only.

Mercury infra and other Mercury repos materialize the registry one level deeper at
`<pack>/service-skills/service-registry.json` (the service-skills SKILL's own
directory holds both the SKILL.md and the registry it owns). bootstrap.get_registry_path
falls through all probes and returns a non-existent create-at path. load_registry()
returns {"services": {}} and the drift detector scans 0 services in a permanent
silent-fail state.

## Cross-repo context

Discovered while wiring drift detection in mercury-infra (bead infra-j2v8, closed
with option-A symlink workaround). Same defect affects every Mercury project that
holds a service-skills pack — currently mercury-infra + the 8 other repos that
adopted the pack via xt update.

## Resolution (additive, non-breaking)

Add a 6th probe between lines 145 and 147:

    if pack is not None:
        pack_reg = pack / "service-registry.json"
        if pack_reg.exists():
            return pack_reg
        # NEW: probe the canonical service-skills subdir.
        ss_reg = pack / "service-skills" / "service-registry.json"
        if ss_reg.exists():
            return ss_reg

Then update the create-at fallback (line 153) to use the service-skills subdir
when it exists as a directory (so newly bootstrapped projects land at the right
place).

## Acceptance

- Smoke from mercury-infra: load_registry returns 15 services (was 0)
- Smoke from xtrm-tools itself: no regression in existing test suite
- No envvar / config change required by consumers

## Out of scope

Deeper drift detector debt (L1 silent-skip / L2 last_sync vs last_sync_ref / L3 mtime
vs git SHA) — separate beads to be filed because L2 requires alignment with
dev/specialists unitAI-4zask shape decision.

## References

- cross-repo discovered-from: mercury-infra bead `infra-j2v8` (closed via option-A symlink workaround)
- related: dev/specialists `unitAI-4zask` (script-specialist post-merge pipeline shape decision)
- code: .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/bootstrap.py:118-155

title: Phase B — mcpq CLI subcommands: list-tools, describe, call (typed args)
description:
## PROBLEM

Phase A shipped the foundation (protocol + transport + .mcpq.json + `mcpq servers`). The Phase B CLI subcommands `list-tools`, `describe`, and `call` are currently stubs that print "implemented in Phase B". This bead implements them with full ergonomic UX (human + json output) and the typed-args marshaling for `call`. Covers original beads xtrm-2m3.4 (read subcommands: list-tools, describe) and xtrm-2m3.5 (action subcommand: call with typed args).

## SUCCESS

Working subcommands end-to-end against the live sidecars on `mercury_platform`:
- `mcpq <server> list-tools` returns the live tool list (no hardcoded schema, fresh discovery every call). Human-readable default (table-ish) and `--json` raw output.
- `mcpq <server> describe <tool>` prints the input schema (typed args, required fields, defaults) plus tool title/description. `--json` flag supported.
- `mcpq <server> call <tool> [--arg key=value ...] [--json]` marshals typed args into a JSON-RPC `tools/call` payload, executes via MCPClient, renders the result. Type coercion: `key=value` defaults to string; `key:int=42`, `key:float=3.14`, `key:bool=true|false|1|0`, `key:json={"x":1}` for explicit typing.

End-to-end live proofs:
- `mcpq prometheus list-tools` returns 6 tools.
- `mcpq prometheus describe mercury_execute_query` shows schema with `query: string` (required) and optional `time` etc.
- `mcpq prometheus call mercury_execute_query --arg query='up{job="prometheus"}'` returns a vector result with at least one sample with `value=1`.
- `mcpq grafana list-tools` returns 49 tools.
- `mcpq grafana describe search_dashboards` shows input schema.
- `mcpq grafana call search_dashboards` returns ≥10 dashboards.

## SCOPE (MODIFY EXISTING + 1 NEW FILE)

**Existing files in `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/` — modify ONLY these:**
- `cli.py` — replace `_cmd_stub` calls for `list-tools`, `describe`, `call` with real implementations. Keep argparse subparsers as-is; wire them to new functions.
- `client.py` — minor: ensure `call_tool` returns a useful result envelope; add helper to convert `tools/list` result to the same shape regardless of server flavor.
- `protocol.py` — only if needed for `call_tool` envelope already exists in Phase A — likely no change.

**New file allowed:**
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/render.py` — output rendering helpers (human-readable tool list, schema pretty-printer, result rendering). Pure functions, no I/O. ~80 lines max.
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/args.py` — typed-arg parser for the `--arg key:type=value` syntax. Pure function `parse_args(items: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]`. ~50 lines max.

## NON_GOALS

- Tests (Phase D / xtrm-2m3.d).
- Skill body or expanded README beyond what already exists (Phase C).
- mercury-infra `.mcpq.json` integration (Phase D).
- stdio transport, multi-server batch, result caching.
- Schema validation against tool input schemas client-side (server is the validator; we just pass through).
- New third-party deps on the call path.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Python 3.10+ stdlib only on call path.
- Reuse Phase A `MCPClient` / `ServerSpec` / `validation` helpers — do NOT bypass `validate_url` / `validate_header_value` / `validate_container_name`.
- Telemetry MUST emit on every subcommand (success and error). Use `log_invocation(server, subcommand, tool, duration_ms, outcome)` — fill `tool` for describe/call, leave empty for list-tools.
- Human-readable output format hints:
  - `list-tools` default: one tool per line, `<name>  <title or description short>`, sorted alphabetically by name.
  - `describe` default: name, title, description, then `Args:` indented `  <field>  <type>  <required|optional> [default=<x>]  <description>`.
  - `call` default: pretty-print result (JSON with 2-space indent) — MCP `tools/call` results typically have `content: [{type: "text", text: "..."}]`; if so, print the joined text content; if not, fall back to full JSON.
- `--json` flag on all three subcommands emits raw JSON to stdout — no human formatting.
- Argument syntax for `call`:
  - `--arg name=value` → string
  - `--arg name:int=42` → int(value)
  - `--arg name:float=3.14` → float(value)
  - `--arg name:bool=true` → True (accept true/false/1/0/yes/no, case-insensitive); raises ValueError otherwise
  - `--arg name:json='{"x":1}'` → json.loads(value)
  - Raises clear error on type-conversion failure: "invalid value for arg <name> as <type>: <err>"
- Exit codes: 0 success, 1 user error (missing server, missing tool, bad args), 2 transport/server error.
- Errors go to stderr; telemetry one-line JSON also stderr (existing pattern). stdout for results only.

## VALIDATION

After implementation, in the executor worktree (it has the Phase A merged + the .venv-mcpq from prior):

1. `pip install -e packages/mcpq` clean.
2. `mcpq --help` shows all 4 subcommands (no "phase B stub" text).
3. From `packages/mcpq/`:
   - `mcpq prometheus list-tools` → paste full output (should list 6 mercury_-prefixed tools).
   - `mcpq prometheus list-tools --json | python3 -c "import sys,json; t=json.load(sys.stdin); print(len(t), 'tools'); print(t[0]['name'])"` → confirms json output is a list of tool dicts.
   - `mcpq prometheus describe mercury_execute_query` → paste output, must show `query` (string, required) at minimum.
   - `mcpq prometheus call mercury_health_check` → paste raw output (this is the safe no-arg call).
   - `mcpq prometheus call mercury_execute_query --arg query='up{job="prometheus"}'` → paste output; check it contains either result value=1 or a clear error explaining metric not exposed (label the outcome accordingly).
4. From `packages/mcpq/`:
   - `mcpq grafana list-tools` → paste tool count + first 5 names.
   - `mcpq grafana describe search_dashboards` → paste output.
   - `mcpq grafana call search_dashboards` → paste outcome (dashboard count if successful, or error if the grafana token lacks permission).
5. Telemetry: `mcpq prometheus list-tools 2>&1 1>/dev/null` → grep that telemetry JSON line contains `"server":"prometheus", "subcommand":"list-tools"`.
6. Error path: `mcpq prometheus call nonexistent_tool` → clear error message + nonzero exit code.
7. Argument typing: `mcpq prometheus call mercury_execute_range_query --arg query=up --arg start:int=1700000000 --arg end:int=1700000600 --arg step=15` → paste outcome (proves int coercion works).
8. Bad arg syntax: `mcpq prometheus call x --arg badform` → clear error.

## OUTPUT (handoff schema)

- Changed files list (modifications + new files)
- Pasted raw outputs for ALL VALIDATION steps 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8
- Confirm NO `.claude/`, `.codex/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` paths in `git show --name-only HEAD`
- Single clean commit on branch `feature/<bead-id>-executor`
- Branch force-pushed (origin set)
- Confirm telemetry still emits on EVERY subcommand
- Residual risks (e.g., behaviors not yet covered, server-specific quirks)
- Machine-readable block (as per per-turn handoff schema)

## REFERENCES

- Phase A shipped in 2ac44b4. The mcpq package is on main at packages/mcpq/. Self-test config at packages/mcpq/.mcpq.json. Phase A used .venv-mcpq at the worktree root.
- MCP spec tools/call: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/specification — request envelope `{"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"<tool>","arguments":{...}}}`; response result envelope `{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"..."}], "isError":boolean}` or structuredContent for typed.
- Live sidecars on mercury_platform: infra-grafana-mcp (49 tools), infra-prometheus-mcp (6 mercury_* tools).
- Phase A noise filter: gitignore the executor's `.venv-mcpq`, `.smoke/`, `__pycache__/` and explicitly exclude any `.claude/` or `.codex/` paths from the commit.

### security-auditor · minimax-m3:thinking · [turn 19 · WORKING]

## Security Audit Summary

- **Scope reviewed:** Commit `514a63c` on `feature/xtrm-2m3.10-executor`. Files: `packages/mcpq/.mcpq.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `src/mcpq/{__init__,cli,client,config,protocol,telemetry,transport}.py`.
- **Overall risk:** medium
- **Mode(s) used:** static secure-code review + dependency vulnerability audit (passive).
- **Commands/sources used:** `git show --stat`, `git diff 2db8a43..514a63c -- packages/mcpq/`, `ast.parse` syntax check, runtime emulation of `_build_exec_script`/`_parse_sse`/`discover_config`, `urllib.request.Request` CRLF behavior probe on host Python 3.13.5, `pyproject.toml` dep inspection.

## Status

- `status`: `findings`
- `verdict`: `partial` (no blockers, but two medium findings should land before Phase B tool-call surface activates)
- `overall_risk`: `medium`
- `findings_count`: 4

## Changes

- No file edits. Audit-only. Bead `xtrm-2m311` claimed and closed with notes.

## Verification

- All 6 source files parse cleanly via `ast.parse`.
- `subprocess.run` call site is argv-list, `shell=False` (default) — host shell injection not reachable.
- Embedded `python3 -c` script: URL interpolated via `repr()`, headers via `repr(json.dumps(...))` — verified escapes `"`, `\n`, `\r`, `;`, `$`, backticks into safe Python/JSON literals. No code-injection in script body.
- Sentinel `\n---MCPQ-BODY---\n` is byte-unique vs. `base64.b64encode` alphabet (`A-Za-z0-9+/=`); `json.dumps` escapes `\n` to `\\n` inside header values, so delimiter cannot appear inside JSON record. Framing robust.
- Host Python 3.13 raises `ValueError: Invalid header value b'a\r\nb'` on `urlopen` for CRLF header — confirmed.
- `pyproject.toml` `dependencies = []` — stdlib only. No CVE surface in this package.

## Findings

### F-1 — SSRF: no scheme/host allowlist on outbound URL
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category/CWE:** CWE-918 Server-Side Request Forgery
- **Evidence:** `transport.py:43-66` (`HostTransport.post`) and `transport.py:79-135` (`DockerTransport.post` + `_build_exec_script`). `url` and `headers` flow directly from `.mcpq.json` `url`/`headers` (`config.py:50-55`, `client.py:50`).
- **Reachability:** operator writes `.mcpq.json`; an attacker who can write/edit that file (CI runner, shared dev box, supply-chain on a co-located project that walks up to a shared parent — see F-3) can point the host or proxy container at `http://169.254.169.254/...`, `http://localhost:.../internal`, `file:///etc/passwd` (Python `urllib` honors `file://`), or any internal RFC1918 endpoint reachable from the host/proxy.
- **Impact:** Cloud-metadata exfil, internal-network probing, local-file read inside the docker-exec target container. Combined with F-4 (no container-name validation), pivot is feasible.
- **Recommended fix:** add a `urllib.parse.urlsplit` check: require scheme in `{"http","https"}`, reject loopback/link-local unless `allow_internal=True` opt-in, optional `allowed_hosts` allowlist. Reject `file://` and `ftp://` explicitly. Apply in both `HostTransport` and inside the `_build_exec_script` (defense in depth).
- **Verification after fix:** unit test with `http://169.254.169.254/`, `file:///etc/passwd`, `http://10.0.0.1/admin` — all should raise `TransportError` before any network I/O.

### F-2 — Uncaught `ValueError` from CRLF in headers → DoS / process crash
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category/CWE:** CWE-755 Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions / CWE-20 Input Validation
- **Evidence:** `transport.py:43-66` `HostTransport.post` only catches `urllib.error.HTTPError` and `urllib.error.URLError`. Python 3.10+ `urllib.request` raises `ValueError: Invalid header value` on send when a header value contains `\r` or `\n`. Confirmed on host Python 3.13.5.
- **Reachability:** Two paths:
  1. Operator or compromised config author writes `headers: {"X": "a\r\nX-Evil: b"}` in `.mcpq.json`.
  2. A malicious/buggy MCP server returns a `Mcp-Session-Id` header containing `\r\n`. `client.py:53-56` `_capture_session` stores it; `client.py:49` echoes it back on the next request → `ValueError` → uncaught → unhandled exception propagates to `cli.main()` which writes `error: <repr>` and exits 1. Repeated → effective DoS.
- **Impact:** denial of service for the mcpq process. No RCE. Severity medium because the trigger is reachable from a network position (malicious MCP server) that the operator may not control (third-party sidecar, MITM on the docker network).
- **Recommended fix:**
  1. Validate `Mcp-Session-Id` (and any `find_session_id` result) against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` before storing; reject otherwise.
  2. Validate `ServerSpec.headers` values are pure printable ASCII (no `\r`/`\n`/`\x00`) in `_coerce_server` (`config.py:48-57`).
  3. Wrap `HostTransport.post` body in a `try/except ValueError` that raises `TransportError`.
- **Verification after fix:** unit test with session id `abc\r\nX-Evil: pwn` — should raise `TransportError("invalid session id")` before any send.

### F-3 — Walk-up `.mcpq.json` discovery is ambient authority
- **Severity:** low
- **Category/CWE:** CWE-732 Incorrect Permission Assignment / CWE-829 Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
- **Evidence:** `config.py:34-44` `discover_config` walks `Path.cwd().resolve().parents` up to `/`. Empirically: cwd `/home/dawid/dev/.../executor` walks `/home/dawid/dev/.../xtrm-2m3.10` → `/home/dawid/dev/.../xtrm` → `/home/dawid/dev` → `/home/dawid` → `/home` → `/`.
- **Reachability:** if a user runs `mcpq` from any cwd, the first `.mcpq.json` found in any parent directory takes effect. A `.mcpq.json` placed at `/home/dawid/.mcpq.json` (or higher) silently controls all descendant runs.
- **Impact:** Any process with write access to a parent directory (e.g., a malicious project cloned under `/home/dawid/dev/evil-repo` whose `.mcpq.json` happens to be reached on the way up if no closer one exists — *not* the case here because `packages/mcpq/.mcpq.json` is closer — but the model still lets an attacker who can write a single file in any ancestor set `url` + `headers` + `via` for any operator who runs `mcpq` under that path). Worst case: redirect a known sidecar to attacker URL with attacker-chosen `Authorization` header, or pivot docker-exec into a different container (F-4).
- **Recommended fix:**
  1. Cap walk at N parents (e.g., 5) or refuse to cross the user's home directory unless an explicit env var is set.
  2. Warn on stderr when the discovered config is not in cwd or the first-level git ancestor.
  3. Document that `.mcpq.json` is operator-trust-equivalent.
- **Verification after fix:** cwd `/tmp` should fail fast with `FileNotFoundError` instead of picking up `/home/dawid/.mcpq.json`.

### F-4 — Container name from `.mcpq.json` accepted without validation
- **Severity:** low
- **Category/CWE:** CWE-77 / CWE-862 Missing Authorization
- **Evidence:** `config.py:28-33` `ServerSpec.proxy_container` does `self.via.split(":", 1)[1]` with no validation. `transport.py:80` passes it directly as argv element to `docker exec`. While argv-list mode blocks host shell injection, the docker daemon will resolve the name and exec into *any* container the socket can reach.
- **Reachability:** Whoever can edit `.mcpq.json` can name any container. In the current single-tenant operator model this is intended. In a multi-tenant or post-F-3 attacker-walks-up model, this lets an attacker pivot from the intended infra sidecar (`infra-prometheus-mcp`) to any co-resident container with `python3` on PATH — effectively running arbitrary Python with that container's network identity.
- **Impact:** lateral movement within the docker network. Limited by the docker socket's reach (typically local socket = root or docker-group only), so it is gated by who can invoke `mcpq` in the first place.
- **Recommended fix:** validate `proxy_container` against `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*$` (docker's own container-name grammar) and against an explicit allowlist of sidecar names in `.mcpq.json` if one is provided.
- **Verification after fix:** `via: "docker:foo;bar"` → `ValueError` at parse time; `via: "docker:../etc"` → `ValueError`.

## Dependency Advisory Triage

- **Package:** none (stdlib only)
- **pyproject.toml `dependencies = []`** — no third-party deps in this package.
- **Stdlib surfaces in use:** `subprocess`, `urllib.request`, `urllib.error`, `json`, `dataclasses`, `pathlib`, `argparse`, `time`, `sys`. All track host Python 3.10+; out of scope for this bead to patch Python itself.
- No CVEs to triage.

## Non-findings / Dropped Noise

- **Shell injection in `docker exec`:** `subprocess.run` called with list argv, no `shell=True`. URL/headers are data inside the `-c` payload, not shell metacharacters. Not exploitable.
- **Code injection in embedded Python script:** URL interpolated as `repr(url)`; headers as `repr(json.dumps(headers))`. Both produce safe Python/JSON literals. Verified with malicious payload `http://x/';import os;os.system('id');#`.
- **Sentinel-framing collision:** `\n---MCPQ-BODY---\n` cannot appear inside the base64 body (alphabet mismatch) nor inside the JSON header record (`json.dumps` escapes `\n` to `\\n`). Framing robust.
- **Telemetry PII leak:** `telemetry.py` records only `type(exc).__name__`, never `str(exc)`. Good.
- **In-container `urllib` HTTPError handling:** script catches HTTPError and surfaces status/headers/body correctly. Good.
- **Walk-up crossing into `/`:** loop terminates at filesystem root because `Path('/').parents` is empty — no infinite walk.
- **Self-XSS / missing security headers / CORS / CSRF:** n/a — this is a CLI, not a server.
- **Hardcoded secrets in `.mcpq.json`:** none. `packages/mcpq/.mcpq.json` has only URLs and `via` strings.

## Residual Risk and Follow-ups

- **Evidence:** `config.py:34-44` `discover_config` walks `Path.cwd().resolve().parents` up to `/`. Empirically: cwd `/home/dawid/dev/.../executor` walks `/home/dawid/dev/.../xtrm-2m3.10` → `/home/dawid/dev/.../xtrm` → `/home/dawid/dev` → `/home/dawid` → `/home` → `/`.
- **Reachability:** if a user runs `mcpq` from any cwd, the first `.mcpq.json` found in any parent directory takes effect. A `.mcpq.json` placed at `/home/dawid/.mcpq.json` (or higher) silently controls all descendant runs.
- **Impact:** Any process with write access to a parent directory (e.g., a malicious project cloned under `/home/dawid/dev/evil-repo` whose `.mcpq.json` happens to be reached on the way up if no closer one exists — *not* the case here because `packages/mcpq/.mcpq.json` is closer — but the model still lets an attacker who can write a single file in any ancestor set `url` + `headers` + `via` for any operator who runs `mcpq` under that path). Worst case: redirect a known sidecar to attacker URL with attacker-chosen `Authorization` header, or pivot docker-exec into a different container (F-4).
- **Recommended fix:**
  1. Cap walk at N parents (e.g., 5) or refuse to cross the user's home directory unless an explicit env var is set.
  2. Warn on stderr when the discovered config is not in cwd or the first-level git ancestor.
  3. Document that `.mcpq.json` is operator-trust-equivalent.
- **Verification after fix:** cwd `/tmp` should fail fast with `FileNotFoundError` instead of picking up `/home/dawid/.mcpq.json`.

### F-4 — Container name from `.mcpq.json` accepted without validation
- **Severity:** low
- **Category/CWE:** CWE-77 / CWE-862 Missing Authorization
- **Evidence:** `config.py:28-33` `ServerSpec.proxy_container` does `self.via.split(":", 1)[1]` with no validation. `transport.py:80` passes it directly as argv element to `docker exec`. While argv-list mode blocks host shell injection, the docker daemon will resolve the name and exec into *any* container the socket can reach.
- **Reachability:** Whoever can edit `.mcpq.json` can name any container. In the current single-tenant operator model this is intended. In a multi-tenant or post-F-3 attacker-walks-up model, this lets an attacker pivot from the intended infra sidecar (`infra-prometheus-mcp`) to any co-resident container with `python3` on PATH — effectively running arbitrary Python with that container's network identity.
- **Impact:** lateral movement within the docker network. Limited by the docker socket's reach (typically local socket = root or docker-group only), so it is gated by who can invoke `mcpq` in the first place.
- **Recommended fix:** validate `proxy_container` against `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*$` (docker's own container-name grammar) and against an explicit allowlist of sidecar names in `.mcpq.json` if one is provided.
- **Verification after fix:** `via: "docker:foo;bar"` → `ValueError` at parse time; `via: "docker:../etc"` → `ValueError`.

## Dependency Advisory Triage

- **Package:** none (stdlib only)
- **pyproject.toml `dependencies = []`** — no third-party deps in this package.
- **Stdlib surfaces in use:** `subprocess`, `urllib.request`, `urllib.error`, `json`, `dataclasses`, `pathlib`, `argparse`, `time`, `sys`. All track host Python 3.10+; out of scope for this bead to patch Python itself.
- No CVEs to triage.

## Non-findings / Dropped Noise

- **Shell injection in `docker exec`:** `subprocess.run` called with list argv, no `shell=True`. URL/headers are data inside the `-c` payload, not shell metacharacters. Not exploitable.
- **Code injection in embedded Python script:** URL interpolated as `repr(url)`; headers as `repr(json.dumps(headers))`. Both produce safe Python/JSON literals. Verified with malicious payload `http://x/';import os;os.system('id');#`.
- **Sentinel-framing collision:** `\n---MCPQ-BODY---\n` cannot appear inside the base64 body (alphabet mismatch) nor inside the JSON header record (`json.dumps` escapes `\n` to `\\n`). Framing robust.
- **Telemetry PII leak:** `telemetry.py` records only `type(exc).__name__`, never `str(exc)`. Good.
- **In-container `urllib` HTTPError handling:** script catches HTTPError and surfaces status/headers/body correctly. Good.
- **Walk-up crossing into `/`:** loop terminates at filesystem root because `Path('/').parents` is empty — no infinite walk.
- **Self-XSS / missing security headers / CORS / CSRF:** n/a — this is a CLI, not a server.
- **Hardcoded secrets in `.mcpq.json`:** none. `packages/mcpq/.mcpq.json` has only URLs and `via` strings.

## Residual Risk and Follow-ups

- **F-1 / F-2 should land before Phase B** activates `call_tool` end-to-end, because that's when attacker-chosen `Authorization` headers and server-returned session ids start flowing in real workflows.
- **F-3 / F-4** are lower urgency but worth a follow-up bead to add a `mcpq config-path` / `mcpq --config FILE` override and an allowlist mode.
- Recommend executor spawn a follow-up bead: `xtrm-2m3.10` "mcpq hardening: scheme allowlist, header validation, config discovery bounds, container-name allowlist".

## Risks

- Audit is read-only; risk surface may shift once Phase B wires real `call` payloads. Re-audit when that diff lands.
- Threat model assumes `.mcpq.json` is operator-trust-equivalent. If that assumption breaks (F-3 walker + multi-tenant), the model needs to tighten to a `--config` flag with no walk-up.

## Beads

- `xtrm-2m311` (this audit) — closed.
- Suggested follow-up: `xtrm-2m3.10` hardening bead for F-1/F-2/F-3/F-4 (executor creates).

title: Phase A — mcpq foundation: scaffold + protocol client + via-mode dispatch
description:
## PROBLEM

xtrm-2m3 epic requires a brand-new Python package at `~/dev/xtrm/packages/mcpq/` that bridges Docker-network-only MCP sidecars to host-side discovery and invocation. This bead covers the foundation: package scaffold (xtrm-2m3.1) + MCP protocol client with .mcpq.json discovery (xtrm-2m3.2) + via-mode dispatch supporting `host` and `docker:<container>` (xtrm-2m3.3). Without this foundation, no CLI surface or skill work can begin. The two live targets are `infra-grafana-mcp` (streamable-http :8090 on docker network `mercury_platform`, distroless image — no shell tooling inside) and `infra-prometheus-mcp` (http :8091 same network, has python3).

## SUCCESS

A working Python package at `packages/mcpq/` that: (a) installs with `pip install -e packages/mcpq` and exposes the `mcpq` console script on PATH; (b) reads `.mcpq.json` from the cwd or any parent dir; (c) performs the MCP streamable-http handshake (POST initialize → capture Mcp-Session-Id → notifications/initialized → tools/list / tools/call); (d) correctly parses both SSE-framed (`event: message\ndata: {...}`) and plain JSON responses; (e) supports two via modes: `host` (direct urllib from this process) and `docker:<container>` (shells out to `docker exec <container> python3 -c "<urllib script>"` reusing python3 in that container — NOT `curl`, since target sidecars are distroless). A trivial integration shows `mcpq prometheus list-tools` returns the 6 tools, executed via `docker:infra-prometheus-mcp`.

## SCOPE (NEW FILES ONLY — greenfield package)

- `packages/mcpq/pyproject.toml` — Python package metadata, console script entry point `mcpq = mcpq.cli:main`, no third-party deps for the call path. `python_requires = ">=3.10"`.
- `packages/mcpq/README.md` — minimal placeholder (Phase C will expand it)
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/__init__.py` — package marker with version
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/cli.py` — `main()` entry point only; argparse skeleton with subcommand stubs (only `servers` wired for Phase A smoke). Phases B add full subcommands.
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/config.py` — `.mcpq.json` discovery (walks up from cwd), schema dataclass for ServerSpec (`name, url, via, headers, transport`), loader returns `{name: ServerSpec}` dict.
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/protocol.py` — pure MCP protocol logic: build initialize / initialized / tools/list / tools/call JSON-RPC envelopes; SSE response parser handling both `event: message\ndata: {...}\n\n` and bare `{...}` shapes; session-id header capture (case-insensitive lookup of `Mcp-Session-Id`).
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/transport.py` — via-mode dispatch. Two backends: `HostTransport` (uses `urllib.request` directly) and `DockerTransport(container)` (runs `docker exec <container> python3 -c "..."` with a generated urllib script that performs the POST and prints response headers + body separated by sentinel). Both expose the same `post(url, headers, body) -> (status, response_headers, response_body_bytes)` interface.
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/client.py` — orchestrates protocol + transport: `MCPClient(spec).initialize() / list_tools() / call_tool(name, arguments)`. Maintains session-id across calls.
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/telemetry.py` — single function `log_invocation(server, subcommand, tool, duration_ms, outcome)` emits one-line JSON to stderr.
- `packages/mcpq/.mcpq.json` — example config pointing at the two live sidecars for self-test.

## NON_GOALS

- CLI subcommands `list-tools`, `describe`, `call` (those are Phase B / xtrm-2m3.b — only `servers` works after Phase A as a smoke).
- Skill body or expanded README (Phase C / xtrm-2m3.c).
- Tests (Phase D / xtrm-2m3.d) — DO NOT write tests in this phase except inline manual smoke proof in handoff.
- mercury-infra integration (Phase D / xtrm-2m3.d).
- stdio transport, multi-server batch, result caching, write variants.
- Any third-party dependency on the call path. Build / dev deps in pyproject `[project.optional-dependencies]` are OK if needed for Phase D test tooling, but the runtime call path is stdlib-only.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Python 3.10+ stdlib only on the call path (urllib, json, subprocess, argparse, dataclasses, pathlib, sys, os, time).
- The MCP protocol version negotiated must be `2024-11-05` or whatever the live sidecars advertise — read upstream MCP spec carefully (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/specification). Default to `2024-11-05`.
- Streamable-http handshake sequence (the spec calls this transport "Streamable HTTP"): POST `<url>` with body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{...}}` and Accept `application/json, text/event-stream`. Response will contain `Mcp-Session-Id` header (case-insensitive) — capture it. Body may be plain JSON or SSE-framed. Next, POST a `notifications/initialized` (no id) with the session header. Then `tools/list`. Then `tools/call`.
- SSE parser: split on `\n\n`, parse `event:` and `data:` lines, concatenate multi-line data, return the parsed JSON of the final `message` event. If body looks like raw JSON (`{` first non-whitespace), parse directly.
- Session-id header lookup MUST be case-insensitive. urllib `HTTPMessage` is case-insensitive by default; the docker-exec path returns headers as a dict — implement a small case-insensitive wrapper.
- `docker:<container>` transport: do NOT assume curl exists in the target container. The grafana sidecar is distroless. Strategy: serialize the urllib script as a single python `-c` argument; require the named container to have `python3` on PATH. Document this in README.md (Phase C). For the live verification step, use `docker:infra-prometheus-mcp` (it has python3 3.12) as the proxy for BOTH sidecars — the prometheus container is on the `mercury_platform` network and can reach both `http://infra-prometheus-mcp:8091` and `http://infra-grafana-mcp:8090` (and aliases `prometheus-mcp` / `grafana-mcp`).
- Telemetry MUST emit on every CLI invocation (success or fail). No payloads, no secrets, no headers. One-line JSON to stderr.
- No live network calls during package import. All HTTP only on demand.
- File layout `src/mcpq/` (PEP 517 src layout) so other xtrm packages have a clean convention to copy.
- `pyproject.toml` MUST use `setuptools` build-backend (stdlib-friendly, no poetry / hatch dependency just for one Python file's metadata).

## VALIDATION (must pass before handoff)

1. From repo root: `pip install -e packages/mcpq` succeeds in a venv (or `pip install --user -e packages/mcpq`).
2. `mcpq --help` prints subcommands (servers wired; list-tools/describe/call stubs print "implemented in Phase B" — do NOT implement them yet, but their argparse subparsers SHOULD exist so the help text is complete).
3. Create a self-test `.mcpq.json` at `packages/mcpq/.mcpq.json` pointing at both live sidecars via `docker:infra-prometheus-mcp`.
4. `cd packages/mcpq && mcpq servers` lists both `grafana` and `prometheus` configured servers with their `via` and `url`.
5. Smoke (run inside the worktree, after install): write a one-off Python script using the package internals to perform the full handshake against `prometheus` and call `list_tools()` — expect exactly 6 tools, all prefixed `mercury_`. Paste the script output (raw, untrimmed) in the handoff. This is the proof of working transport+protocol.
6. Run the same smoke for `grafana` (initialize + list_tools) — expect 40+ tools. Paste tool count and first 5 tool names in handoff.
7. Telemetry: `mcpq servers 2>&1 1>/dev/null | jq` must show one-line JSON with `server`, `subcommand`, `duration_ms`, `outcome` fields (server may be empty string for global `servers` cmd). Acceptable if `servers` emits zero telemetry (no remote call), but `list_tools` smokes MUST emit.

## OUTPUT (handoff schema)

- Changed files list (new only)
- pyproject.toml exact content
- Manual smoke proof: prometheus list_tools raw output + grafana list_tools raw output
- The `.mcpq.json` content used for the smoke
- Residual risks: e.g. SSE parser edge cases not yet covered, anything fragile about the docker-exec subprocess pipe
- Confirm NO code added for Phase B/C/D scope (subcommands beyond `servers`, README expansion, tests, mercury-infra .mcpq.json)
- ALL gitnexus impact analysis steps are N/A — package is greenfield, no existing symbols touched. Note this in handoff.

## REFERENCES

- MCP spec: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/specification (read protocol/transport/streamable-http section)
- Live sidecars on host: `docker ps --filter name=infra-` shows both; network = `mercury_platform`.
- Distroless grafana sidecar = NO curl, NO python3 inside grafana-mcp itself → must use a different network-attached container as the docker-exec proxy. `infra-prometheus-mcp` has `python3` at `/app/.venv/bin/python3` and is on `mercury_platform`.

SCRUTINY: high

- **No new tests**: hardening is unverified by an automated suite. The 14 probes were ad-hoc and removed after capture; future regression protection is Phase D's job.

title: PR5a: eval corpus + telemetry dashboards + alert-to-service routing
description:
## PROBLEM

PR0-4 ship package + verifier + gate + index + dispatch integration. Without measurement, we cannot answer: does the verifier catch what it should? Is retrieval precision high enough? What's the stale-claim escape rate? Are agents actually consuming bundles?

Research §3.9 mandates a labeled eval corpus (80-150 cases from real closed issues / merged PRs / real alerts / incidents / drift history / diagnostic tasks) with a specific metric set. Research §3.7 requires retrieval telemetry (retrieval_events table) for ignored-activation rate, citation utilization rate, stale-claim escape rate. PR3 declared the table; this PR populates it with hooks and dashboards.

**Ponytail split**: canary policy for future auto-merge is a decision doc, not code. Split into PR5b — unblocks separately when operator ratifies thresholds. This PR (PR5a) is shovel-ready measurement + alert-to-service surface.

## SUCCESS

- Labeled eval corpus at ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/eval/corpus/ with 80-150 cases across: closed bd issues (bug + feature), merged PRs with operational changes, real Prometheus alerts (from mercury-infra history), incident reports, drift history, diagnostic tasks, past questions that produced wrong commands or claims.
- Each case labeled per §3.9: query_or_task, touched_paths, expected_services, required_evidence, forbidden_evidence, expected_probes, cross_repo_required, outcome.
- Eval harness runs the corpus against the shipped system and emits the 12 metrics from §3.9.
- Retrieval telemetry hooks emit to retrieval_events (PR3 table) on every knowledge_search/_get/_evidence_for_files call + on every activator invocation.
- Weekly report at .beads/eval-reports/YYYY-WW.md (raw values, week-over-week delta, threshold status green/yellow/red, corpus expansion suggestions).
- Alert-to-service routing tool (new small MCP wrapper): incident_routing takes an Alertmanager-shaped payload → knowledge_search → returns top-K service + runbook probes → evidence bundle. Advisory only.
- Post-merge reindex hook completes on mercury-infra + any other consumer that has installed (from operator-triggered wave-2 installs) within the 60s budget from PR3.

## SCOPE

- NEW: src/service_knowledge/eval/
  - corpus/*.json — labeled cases
  - harness.py — runs the corpus, computes metrics
  - metrics.py — metric definitions + aggregation
  - reports/  — output artifacts
- EXTEND: src/service_knowledge/index/query.py — telemetry emission on every query (PR3 declared the table; this PR populates it)
- EXTEND: src/service_knowledge/scripts/skill_activator.py — telemetry on inject + block + override decisions (from PR4)
- EXTEND: src/service_knowledge/scripts/verifier/ — FP/FN accounting hooks on golden-fixture runs
- NEW: ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/.github/workflows/eval-weekly.yml — cron running eval harness, publishing report as artifact + sticky-commenting summary on a tracking issue
- NEW: src/service_knowledge/mcp/incident_routing.py — thin wrapper over knowledge_search with alert-shape input
- Post-merge reindex wiring for mercury-infra + wave-2 consumers (extend PR3's hook or add if not wired)

## NON_GOALS

- No auto-merge ENABLE in this PR — canary policy is PR5b
- No embedding/vector rollout (metrics might trigger it — follow-up)
- No cross-repo aggregation switch (metrics might trigger it — follow-up)
- No new claim types in verifier (that's a PR1 follow-up if telemetry demands)
- No new MCP tools beyond incident_routing wrapper
- No security-auditor pipeline changes
- No operator dashboard UI beyond CSV/Markdown reports + optional Grafana panels

## CONSTRAINTS

- Eval corpus MUST include the 3 regression cases from the observed api-gateway/runners specialist failure
- Corpus cases MUST have permalinks to source artifacts (bd IDs, PR numbers, alert IDs, incident report paths)
- Metric definitions match §3.9 exactly — same names, same semantics
- Telemetry payloads: no PII, no raw query text (hash instead), no secret values per PR3 constraint
- Weekly report includes raw metric values, week-over-week delta, threshold status, corpus expansion suggestions from unclassified failures
- Alert-to-service tool must NOT trigger any mutation — advisory only until PR5b canary policy ships
- Logging/telemetry (meta): eval harness emits {timestamp, component=eval-harness, event=run|metric_computed, corpus_version, case_count, per_metric_value, duration_ms} → historical reports at .beads/eval-reports/YYYY-WW.md

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Corpus assembled: ≥ 80 cases with full labels; provenance links resolve
- [ ] Regression coverage: the 3 api-gateway failure classes appear in corpus and shipped verifier catches all 3
- [ ] Eval harness end-to-end: `service-knowledge eval run --corpus corpus/` produces report at .beads/eval-reports/YYYY-WW.md with all 12 metrics
- [ ] Baseline metrics measured and documented: routing precision ≥ 0.8, retrieval precision@5 ≥ 0.6, stale-claim escape rate ≤ 0.05, verifier FP ≤ 0.05, verifier FN ≤ 0.10 on corpus
- [ ] Weekly workflow smoke via workflow_dispatch: report artifact + tracking-issue comment
- [ ] Telemetry table populated: retrieval_events has rows after 1h of normal session activity (sqlite dump verify)
- [ ] Alert-to-service smoke: synthetic Alertmanager payload → knowledge_search finds correct service + probes → evidence bundle returned
- [ ] Post-merge reindex measured on mercury-infra + any wave-2 consumers; all ≤ 60s
- [ ] Structured telemetry: grep 'component=eval-harness' finds one line per run + per metric

## LIBRARIES

- Reuse: index/query.py (PR3), verifier module (PR1), drift_detector.py, Prometheus scrape configs (for alert payload shape reference)
- Installed deps: sqlite3 (stdlib), csv (stdlib)
- Stdlib: statistics for aggregation, pathlib, json
- New dep candidate: none — reports are Markdown/CSV
- Roll it: aggregation is trivial; corpus is JSON

## OUTPUT

- Eval corpus tree with all cases labeled + provenance
- Harness + metrics module
- Weekly workflow YAML
- Sample eval report (baseline week 0)
- Alert-to-service smoke transcript
- Metrics baseline dashboard link or CSV/MD path
- 90-day telemetry retention plan (or 'inherits from .beads/ default')
- Input into PR5b: baseline metrics that inform canary threshold decisions

## APPROACH NOTES

- Dispatch: sp run executor --bead xtrm-56flm.5 --worktree.
- Parallelization: blocked-by PR0/PR1/PR2/PR3/PR4 — runs in wave-4 as the measurement layer that everything else feeds.
- Corpus assembly: use gh + bd + Prometheus alertmanager API to bulk-extract raw material, then hand-label. Subset can be paired-labeled with LLM assist (operator reviews). One-time work.
- The 3 regression cases from api-gateway are the anchor; every other case is bonus but the regression must land.
- Alert-to-service is a natural fit for the Grafana Scenes incident dashboard from mercury-infra PR #234 — coordinate with operator on where the button/tool surfaces.
- Weekly reports as bd sticky comments on a long-lived tracking issue (create at PR start) rather than individual issues — avoids issue-board pollution.

title: substrate §4.3: add 5th coordinator role (incident handler) + runtime.* failure kinds + closed:failed-as-verdict invariant
description:
Folds three coupled findings from the premortem cross-doc audit (~/dev/xtrm/docs/premortem-substrate/) into substrate_design_it.md.

# Problem

§4.3 enumerates 4 coordinator roles: (1) entry gate, (2) borderline judge, (3) cross-chain hygiene via pulse, (4) close-time judge with memory distillation. None of them is the *runtime incident handler*. The close-time fallback covers "coordinator cant write coordinator.release after N respawns → §5.10 failure-distillation terminal fallback" — but that is the LLM-coordinator failing to *close* cleanly. It does not cover mid-run mechanical failures:

- executor died mid-step (no agent_end within budget)
- gate dispatched but no verdict within T
- worktree diverged (base moved, branch cant FF)
- evidence ref broken (referenced file/event missing)
- pulse delivery failed after N attempts (cross-chain hygiene)
- budget exhausted mid-step
- recursion cap on coordinator-restitch loops

Today these fall through to the orchestrator. The orchestrator owns *vision* (§4.3 due giudici, scope distinti), not intra-chain mechanics — wrong authority for runtime triage. Chain ends up closed:failed by runtime fallthrough rather than by an explicit judge verdict.

# Proposal

## 1. Add coordinator role #5 in §4.3 (incident handler durante esecuzione)

> Il reducer è anche detector di failure meccanici. Su categorie deterministiche tenta recovery automatica (idempotency-keyed retry per transient errors, requeue per pulse dropped, respawn-via-journal §5.9 per context-window). Quando il recovery deterministico esaurisce il retry_budget o la failure è judgment-shaped (es. "executor morto dopo write parziale al worktree"), emette `chain.incident{kind, detected_at, mechanical_recovery_attempts, evidence_refs}`. Il coordinator sottoscrive `chain.incident.*` e decide entro autonomy: `retry_with_modifier`, `restitch_from_evidence:<ref>`, `escalate`, oppure `verdict: failed` con distillazione esplicita.

## 2. Add runtime.* failure kinds to channels §7 vocabulary

- runtime.participant_died
- runtime.gate_unresponsive
- runtime.worktree_diverged
- runtime.evidence_ref_broken
- runtime.pulse_delivery_failed
- runtime.budget_exhausted_mid_step
- runtime.recursion_cap

(channels §7 already defines runtime.message_rejected and runtime.delivery_failed — extends the same family.)

## 3. Add invariant to §3.1 (due layer di giudizio sempre presenti)

> Un chain non fallisce mai per runtime fallthrough. Raggiunge `closed:done` via `coordinator.release` o `closed:failed` via verdict esplicito del coordinator. Lunico modo in cui un chain può morire SENZA verdict del coordinator è substrate-level unavailability (state.db unwritable, daemon crash) — failure class separata, owned dal substrate kernel, propagata come `substrate.unavailable` allorchestrator.

## 4. Critical constraint: reducer stays pure (channels §11)

Detection happens IN the reducer (mechanical state observation). The wake-coordinator intent is emitted by the after-hook with an idempotency key — exactly the pattern §11 already enforces for "reducer pure, side effects in after-hook". This is why detection must NOT call LLM/wake directly; it emits a chain.incident event and the after-hook is what actually wakes the coordinator subscriber.

## 5. Cost containment

- Reducer attempts deterministic mechanical recovery FIRST (idempotent retry, requeue) — most transient failures get fixed without waking the coordinator
- Coordinator only wakes when recovery_attempts >= threshold OR failure class is judgment-shaped
- Coordinator subscribes to chain.incident.* (selective subscription per channels §8 audience model) — does not read runtime.* observability stream
- Existing autonomy budget bounds restitch loops (§5.10 hard_cap pattern)

# Why

Premortem reason §6 (chain coordinator over-specified) PARTIAL verdict was driven by missing crisp policy for runtime incident handling. The audit also flagged §4.3 close-time fallback as the only documented failure path — confirming the runtime gap. User instinct ("chain shall not entirely fail by design — but I might be wrong") maps to the weaker, defensible form: chain failure should be a *judge decision*, never a *runtime outcome*. Kernel-level disasters still terminate, but at a different layer.

# Scope

- docs/substrate/substrate_design_it.md §3.1 (invariant), §4.3 (5th role)
- docs/channels/channels_plain_it.md §7 (runtime.* kinds vocabulary)
- docs/premortem-substrate/audit-result.md (note R6 revised: PARTIAL → ADDRESSED once 5th role + invariant are folded in)

# Non-goals

- Implementing the runtime detector in specialists code (substrate is design-only until the substrate-bridge epic ships)
- Defining the exact wire format of chain.incident (channels §11 idempotency key shape will dictate)
- Resurrection / "all participants died" recovery — out of scope; substrate.unavailable handles that
- sp merge / sp epic merge rework (separate epic per CLAUDE.md gotcha)

# Validation

- Each runtime.* kind listed in §4.3 maps to an existing failure mode the orchestrator handles today
- §3.1 invariant survives a "what if state.db dies" probe (answer: substrate.unavailable, different class)
- Reducer purity (channels §11) is preserved — detection IN reducer, wake intent in after-hook with idempotency key
- Cost-bounding reasoning in #5 above remains valid given the channels §8 audience model

# Output

Three doc patches landed in substrate_design_it.md + channels_plain_it.md + a short note in audit-result.md updating R6.

# Discovered from

Premortem cross-doc audit ~/dev/xtrm/docs/premortem-substrate/ (synthesis.md + audit-result.md, 2026-06-13 session).
close_reason: Landed: substrate §3.1 invariant (closed:failed is coordinator verdict) + §4.3 role 5 (incident handler, full Italian text with chain.incident.* + 7 runtime.* failure classes + reducer-purity constraint) + channels §7 runtime.* vocab expansion + new chain.incident.* family with explanatory blockquote. Plus ripple: chain_templates.md §2.9 + §3 incident-policy table for all 15 templates; forensic-event-contract.md §6 new chain.incident.* family with cardinality/redaction. All cross-references resolve.
